An overview of the UK’s
Software-as-a-Service sector

The Saas Brief [Ge

Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) is a technology distribution model where
software is hosted by a third-party and accessed via the cloud. This technology
is often licensed on a subscription basis, for example the Beauhurst platform.
The popularity of this sector has grown rapidly, with over 2,000 ambitious SaaS
companies spread across the UK.

The sector encompasses software companies operating in a whole range of
specialities, from fintech to adtech to artificial intelligence. Almost 15% of all
fundraisings since 2011 have been secured by SaaS companies, making it a
critical sector in the Uk’s high-growth ecosystem.

There are 2,245 active, ambitious SaaS
companies in the UK.

An additional 203 have exited the market,
either through an IPO or an acquisition,
and 383 are no longer trading.

The sector is dominated by seed and
venture stage companies (64%). Exit and
death rates are very similar to
sector-agnostic figures, but - as with other
tech sectors — there are significantly fewer
companies at the established stage.
